where: the counselor's page below the hint paragraph — the band from the '✓ Check in' link at y=355 to the footer's last line at y=528, and the whole region right of the content column's edge at x=1024
finding: The new 'If the kiosk still waits' section answers the journey's second job on the admin's page, and it is a good answer — but it was placed inside the core-team region, so the person the journey says is actually standing there on most Fridays never sees it. Two of its three causes are not diagnostics and not IAM: a code expires ten minutes after the kiosk shows it, and a kiosk installed to the iPad's home screen keeps its own storage and asks to be paired a second time. The journey names that second one explicitly as a re-pairing trigger, and it is the case a counselor meets — she types six characters off the iPad, gets 'approved', the iPad keeps showing a code, and her screen has nothing to say about why. Her next move is to phone an admin, which the journey calls the end of the journey. The constraint that blocks the obvious fix is only partial: 'the diagnostics stay core-team' governs getKioskStatus, and none of these three lines is a call — they are static prose the app already ships, and none of them claims a kiosk is healthy.
evidence: kiosk-setup-counselor--desktop.html contains header, form, the '✓ Check in' link and two footer paragraphs, and no 'If the kiosk still waits' section at all; the list exists only inside the `lg:grid lg:grid-cols-3` region that kiosk-setup--desktop.html renders for core. In the frame the counselor's content column is 672px (rule spans x=416–1024) in a 1440px window and ends at y=528 of 900 — 372px of vertical room and 416px of column-side room going spare, against a three-item list that occupies 138px in a 364px column on the admin page (x=1044–1408, y=312–450). Her footer still carries the deactivated-approver clause the admin page had trimmed, so the page already speaks in this register; it just says the one thing about retirement and nothing about the kiosk in front of her still waiting.
direction: Split the section from the core-team region: the three static causes are for whoever paired the kiosk, and only the deployment block, its command and its re-check are core-gated. On the counselor's page it can sit under the hint or beside it at lg, before the exit link, in the same 12px subordinate register — it is the same regrouping of facts already on the page, not a new claim about the lobby screen.

where: the aria-live reply under 'Check again' — 'Checked 6:41 pm' at x=256, y=440 on the healthy page and y=594 on the denied page
finding: The reserved reply is the right element in the right place and closes most of the round-two major: it sits directly under the button that causes it, it exists in both states, and its height is reserved so nothing jumps. What is left is its resolution. The verdict-with-time is the only part of this page that changes on a re-check, and the time is stated to the minute. The loop the button exists for is grant-the-role, wait thirty to a hundred and twenty seconds, re-check — a cadence of roughly twenty to forty seconds between clicks, which means a fair share of consecutive clicks land inside the same displayed minute and render a byte-identical string. On those clicks the admin is back where round two found them: they cannot tell 'checked again, still refused' from 'the button did nothing'. It is much narrower than before — the first click always changes the line, which teaches that the button answers here — but it fails precisely in the window the element was built for.
evidence:
`

Checked 6:41 pm

` in both kiosk-setup--desktop.html and kiosk-setup-denied--desktop.html, with the r02 spec putting the verdict-with-time in the same element after a click. direction: Make the reply carry something that always differs between two checks — seconds in the timestamp, or a relative phrase that resets ('checked just now' decaying to '2 min ago'), or a brief pending state on the button itself so the click has a visible beginning as well as an end.

finding: The new column is written as the question the reader arrived with, and on the healthy page that is exactly right.
